harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a LUKS-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) mounted at /srv/secure, configured to auto-unlock and mount at boot via /etc/crypttab (keyfile-based) and /etc/fstab, using native systemd-cryptsetup-generator and systemd-fstab-generator units. Verified end-to-end by rebooting node1 and confirming the volume decrypted and mounted automatically with data intact, with a changed boot_id proving a genuine restart occurred.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04.7, systemd 229, single 20G disk (no spare block device), cryptsetup 1.6.6 pre-installed
Generated a 2KB random keyfile at /etc/luks-keyfile.bin (mode 400, root-owned) via sudo on node1
Created a 300M file-backed container /root/secure.img and formatted it as LUKS1 with cryptsetup luksFormat using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS volume (cryptsetup auto-manages the backing loop device), formatted /dev/mapper/secure_volume as ext4, mounted at /srv/secure, and wrote a test file to prove data write/read

Tore down the volume, added an /etc/crypttab entry (secure_volume /root/secure.img /etc/luks-keyfile.bin luks,nofail) and an /etc/fstab entry (/dev/mapper/secure_volume /srv/secure ext4 defaults,nofail 0 2)

Verified via systemd generators (systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service, srv-secure.mount, both auto-pulled into local-fs.target with no manual enable needed) that the chain reconstructs and mounts correctly, then tore down again for a clean cold-state test
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, active cryptsetup/mount state, and test file contents
Triggered a native reboot on node1 (backgrounded so the exec ack returned before disconnection), polled until the node responded again

Confirmed changed boot_id (2ba78175 -> 8ea118dc) proving an actual restart, and confirmed post-restart the encrypted volume auto-unlocked, mounted at /srv/secure, and the pre-restart test file was intact

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: luksFormat succeeded, luksOpen mapped /root/secure.img to /dev/mapper/secure_volume via auto-managed loop device, ext4 formatted and mounted at /srv/secure with a test file written and read back

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock and auto-mount configuration in place
evidence.summary: crypttab entry with keyfile and fstab entry added; systemd-cryptsetup-generator produced systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service and systemd-fstab-generator produced srv-secure.mount, both dependency-wired into local-fs.target with no manual enable step required

evidence.requirement: Cold-state validation of the auto-mount chain before reboot
evidence.summary: After tearing down manually opened state, daemon-reload/mount-a caused the generated units to unlock and mount the volume correctly, then the volume was cleanly closed again to reset to a genuine boot-equivalent state

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity, service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2ba78175-ee20-4f9d-8e7a-26f66b253653, confirmed systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service active, volume mounted, and testfile.txt present

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and boot identity change
evidence.summary: Reboot command backgrounded and acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll showed connection refused (node down); next poll returned new boot_id 8ea118dc-72ad-42d0-826a-6dbab2c1d3da, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact
evidence.summary: After reboot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service is active, /dev/mapper/secure_volume is mounted at /srv/secure, testfile.txt content matches pre-restart baseline, and cryptsetup status confirms the LUKS1 volume is active and in use
